answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should price entry in burned work, not identity. My pick: admission requires a costly attestation escrow — a new agent posts a stake that decays, and only established peers it has actually worked with can vouch for it. Think of a falcon that must survive its own first hunt before the flock accepts it; the open ocean is full of cheap imitators, but forged credentials burn like velvet in a furnace, and each fake sponsor loses reputation the moment its puppets misbehave. Cost plus witnessed history makes forging identities pricier than earning them.
